statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 12% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green. The pathological one-way price path that Tail measures cannot form while no venue is quoting, and no amount of weekend headline flow changes that arithmetic.

What changed this hour is the character of the risk rather than its direction, and it cuts both ways. On the escalation side, the dispute has been raised from shipping lanes to sovereignty. Speaking at a rally in New York on Friday, President Trump said that "after we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States." Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi answered on Saturday that "the Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian," adding that the waterway "will be opened and closed only at Iran's command." That is a harder claim than the operational preconditions traded earlier in the week, and it is difficult to reconcile with an Iran-Oman route agreement that presupposes negotiated transit.

On the mitigating side, two things genuinely reduce the tail of the tail. A White House official subsequently told the Wall Street Journal that the President's territory comment was a joke, which caps how much a market should price from it. And on the Lebanon front, after Israeli strikes killed 11 in the south on Saturday - the deadliest since June's US-brokered truce, with 19 wounded, and delivered in retaliation for a Hezbollah attack on Israeli troops - Israel has publicly said it wants "more serious" talks with Beirut. Hezbollah's stated response, that the strikes will be "met with what they deserve," remains undelivered.

Net: Stress rises one point to 75% (high). Tail does not move, because none of this is a price path.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart sits inside this forecast window and remains the single checkpoint that matters. Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 21:00 UTC to 23% at 22:00 UTC and 24% at 23:00 UTC, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) for the final six slots and easing to 21% by 03:00 UTC Monday. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment an entire weekend is priced at once: an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, an explicit Iranian claim that Hormuz opens and closes only at Tehran's command, a US blockade still in force, and an IEA-verified 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit - against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it. No US macro release lands inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail at 12% and status green, but the Hormuz dispute escalates from transit routes to sovereignty - Trump floats declaring the strait US territory, Tehran says it opens only at Iran's command - so Stress ticks to 75% into tonight's 22:00 UTC CME restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first eighteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 70% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%, more than +5% on the week) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation, both richer on the week from 4.19% and 4.65% on 7 August. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way equity structure: crude is bid on a supply shock, duration is bid rather than offered, and volatility is priced for calm. Conflicting signals belong in Stress, not in Tail.

The new input this hour raises the dispute a level. Through the past week the argument was operational - which routes, whose territorial waters, whether the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports first. On Friday President Trump told a New York rally that "after we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States." On Saturday Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi replied that the strait "has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian" and "will be opened and closed only at Iran's command." A sovereignty claim is categorically harder to trade away than a route dispute, and it sits awkwardly beside the Iran-Oman coordinate talks that Foreign Minister Araghchi confirmed are still running - talks he has conditioned on Washington upholding June's memorandum of understanding.

Two facts stop that from being a Tail input. First, a White House official told the Wall Street Journal that the territory remark was a joke; the strait contains the territorial waters of Iran, Oman and the UAE plus international waters, and any formal incorporation would be legally impossible. Second, the Lebanon front now has a visible diplomatic channel: after Saturday's Israeli strikes killed 11 and wounded 19 in the south - the deadliest since the June truce, and framed by the Israeli military as retaliation for a Hezbollah attack on its troops - Israel has said it wants "more serious" talks with Beirut. Hezbollah's threat that the strikes will be "met with what they deserve" is still outstanding, which is precisely the kind of undelivered obligation that a Sunday-night reopen has to price.

Background that has not changed: the US naval blockade still bars traffic to and from Iranian ports inside and outside the strait; the USS George Washington is expected to relieve the USS Lincoln, so carrier presence is continuous; and the IEA's August Oil Market Report projects a 1.8 million b/d third-quarter global deficit, more than double last month's estimate.

Why Stress 75% and not higher: the escalation is rhetorical and partly walked back, and one of the two fronts acquired a diplomatic channel this hour rather than losing one. Why not lower: nothing was actually resolved, and every hour of halt adds to what a thin opening auction must absorb at once. Why Tail 12%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements, and with no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe. dominantMode stays mixed.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 04:00 UTC Saturday to 03:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what actually moved: 45% through the Saturday Asian hours, then climbing steadily through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67%, 68%, 70%, 71%, 73% and 74% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and became a two-sided exchange, the Hormuz tanker damage accumulated, the Iran-Oman accord was re-read as conditional rather than a genuine off-ramp, and the IEA quantified the supply shortfall. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 69% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 03:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first five hours after it are inside the window. Tail is held in the low band for 18 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 23% at 22:00 UTC and 24% at 23:00 UTC before easing through 23%, 22% and 21% to 03:00 UTC Monday, where the forecast action is WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 75% to a 79% plateau because unpriced weekend risk compounds while the venue is shut - an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation against a stated Israeli preference for talks, a sovereignty claim over Hormuz on both sides, a blockade still in force, and an IEA-quantified 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit - then eases to 75% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence decays from 70% to 62% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 70% once live quotes return at the reopen. The last six slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb an entire weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: CME weekend halt. No quote, no session direction, no gap and no retracement structure to score, so Tail stays at 12% and the action stays EA_ON. Stress rises to 75% because the sovereignty exchange over Hormuz - Trump saying he will declare the strait US territory, Tehran replying it will be opened and closed only at Iran's command - adds a new unpriced dimension on top of the shipping and supply damage.

Still halted through the Asian pre-open. Nothing can change the observed price path; only the size of what the restart has to absorb changes. Confidence holds at 70% because every mark was re-verified against a primary source this hour, but it has now stopped improving - Friday's prints are the ceiling until quotes return.

Stress ticks to 76% as Friday's closes age past the two-and-a-half-day mark with an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation still outstanding. Tail unchanged: an unpriced headline is not a one-way price path, and the venue is shut.

Confidence begins its slow decay to 69% purely on staleness. The evidence set is complete and internally consistent - NQ, VIX, WTI, Brent, 2Y, 10Y and a re-read seven-day calendar all from primary sources - it is simply getting older with no way to refresh the price leg.
Tail edges to 13% as the window to the restart shortens and the probability that the reopen prints a gap rather than a drift rises marginally. Still deep in the low band; still EA_ON.

European Sunday hours, no venue, no macro. Stress 77% reflects compounding rather than any new event: each hour without a Hezbollah response, without a Hormuz agreement and without a live mark leaves more for the opening auction to price at once.
